case_name: Reliance Energy Limited and Another v Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation
respondent:
Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation
Supreme Court of India

11 September 2007
CIVIL APPEAL NO.3526 of 2007
The Judgment was delivered by: S. H. Kapadia, J.

facts: The State of Maharashtra through Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation Ltd. (for short, 'MSRDC') floated Global Tender for completing Mumbai Trans Harbour Link ('MTHL') between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai on BOT basis.
Reliance Energy Limited is a company registered under the Companies Act, 1956. It is engaged in generation, transmission and disbursement of power in Maharashtra, Delhi etc.
HDEC is a company incorporated in Korea. It is specialized in construction of bridges.
The bidders were required to submit RFQ Document by 10.1.2005.
REL/HDEC formed a consortium. As a consortium they were required to comply with cl. 7.2.2 which stipulated net cash profit at Rs. 200 crores.
The said consortium has been excluded from the second stage of bidding on the ground that it has not fulfilled the said criteria mentioned in cl. 7.2.2.
REL/HDEC had submitted their RFQ Document on 9.1.2005.
HDEC had undertaken construction contracts in Iraq. On account of war in Iraq their annual report for the year 2001 showed negative income.
issues: The objective of the Pre-Qualification is to qualify the applicants that have the necessary experience and financial and technical capabilities to undertake the work for which the Request for Proposal is to be invited.
What are the criteria for evaluating a consortium's financial capability?
How should the net cash profit and net worth of the consortium be calculated?
court_reasoning: The court held that the exclusion of REL/HDEC from the second stage of bidding was justified as they had not fulfilled the criteria mentioned in cl. 7.2.2.
The court noted that the consortium's financial statements showed a negative income for the year 2001, but subsequent years showed positive net profits.
The court concluded that the exclusion of REL/HDEC was reasonable and did not violate any principles of natural justice.
holding: The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal filed by Reliance Energy Limited and upheld the decision of the lower court to exclude REL/HDEC from the second stage of bidding.
